fieldMarks: 300-500 mm body with only a 10-25 mm furred tail; about 800 g
Blackish, very coarse fur with a small white spot at the base of each ear
behavior: Mostly fossorial and more active at night; tunnels along stream banks
Not aquatic or arboreal, though it swims and can climb
Eats ferns and other vegetation and stores haypiles for winter; active through the winter
Usually solitary, sometimes in loose colonies
habitat: Damp ravines and shaded slopes in coastal and montane conifer forest with dense ground cover, often near watercourses.
range: Southwestern British Columbia south along the Cascade, Olympic, Coast and Siskiyou ranges to central California and the Sierra Nevada.
